subject: Trial evaluation approach: shadow vs simulated-batch playbook
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Natalie Park <natalie@healthsync.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + decision needed: evaluation approach and success criteria

Hi Natalie — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of the items we agreed and a couple of decision points we need from you to lock the trial plan:

Summary from today's call
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference integration for triage and summarization across HealthSync's provider notes. Success metric is a measurable uplift in triage precision with acceptable latency under 600ms 95th percentile.
- Scope: ~2k daily documents (initial sample), PII controls via customer-managed keys, and audit logging.

Decision items (we need your preference so we can finalize the runbook)
1) Evaluation methodology (choose one):
   a) Offline simulated-batch: we run model variants on a historical dataset (you provide 2 weeks of de-identified notes + gold labels) and score using the rubric in the attached workbook. Fast, safe, good for surface-level quality/recall checks.
   b) Live shadow: run Redwood in shadow mode against a small production stream for 1 week to capture latency, KV caching behavior, and real-world distribution shifts. Stronger ops validation, requires one week of sampling and access to the streaming endpoint.

2) Success criteria (drafted in attachment): precision >= 82%, recall >= 75% on triage labels; hallucination rate < 2% sampled; 95th pctl latency < 600ms. Open to tweaks from your clinical QA.

3) Owners: we propose
   - Evaluation lead (metrics & rubric): Karthik Iyer
   - Trial ops / infra liaison: Ben Carter
   - Customer success / rollout owner on your side: Natalie (HealthSync)

Next steps if you confirm the evaluation path today:
- If you pick offline simulated-batch: HealthSync provides de-identified sample + gold labels and we deliver a scored report in 5 business days.
- If you pick live shadow: we schedule a 1-week shadow window (we'll need an ops contact + sampling window) and deliver a combined quality + ops report 7 calendar days after the window.

Attachments: HealthSync-POC-success-criteria.xlsx (draft), evaluation-rubric-v1.md

Asking for: please reply with your preferred evaluation methodology and any tweaks to the success criteria by EOD Monday so we can book the runbook items.

—
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Natalie Park <natalie@healthsync.com>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + decision needed: evaluation approach and success criteria

+1 to the approach; a couple of suggestions to make the evaluation deliverable more actionable for HealthSync's clinical reviewers:
1) Recommend a hybrid path (offline -> shadow) as a default: start with simulated-batch so we can iterate quickly on prompt templates and label mapping, then follow with a targeted 5-business-day shadow to validate latency, memory/kv cache behavior and low-probability failure modes. This minimizes Ops risk while still getting real-world signals.

2) Rubric tweaks (attached updated):
   - Add per-intent F1 and a confusion matrix for the top 5 triage labels.
   - Add a qualitative hallucination review: 100-sample human audit across edge cases and a short narrative on root causes.
   - Add cost-per-inference estimate across model variants (to aid procurement).

3) Proposed owners (internal):
   - Evaluation lead (metrics & rubric): Karthik Iyer (I'll drive scoring & the report)
   - Trial Ops: Ben Carter (scheduling, endpoint config, sampling)
   - CSM liaison: Marissa Cole (deployment coordination & acceptance)

I can produce the first offline run if Natalie can provide the de-identified set and labels by Wednesday. If not, we can pivot to scheduling the shadow for next Monday.

Karthik
Lead, Applied ML | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai

All — operational notes and timeline from my side if we go hybrid (offline -> 5-day shadow):

Plan & timeline (hybrid)
- Day 0 (kickoff): finalize dataset access, SSO keys, and sampling window. DocuSign SOW link will be circulated after we confirm owners.
- Days 1–3: offline simulated-batch run on the provided historical dataset. Deliverables: scored spreadsheet, per-intent confusion matrix, cost estimate.
- Days 4–5: iterate on prompts and mappings based on offline results.
- Week 2 (Monday–Friday): 5-business-day shadow at 5% sample rate (configurable). Daily ops sync and health checks. Final combined report 7 calendar days after shadow completes.

Ops requirements
- Minimal STS access for one service account + endpoint allowlist for HealthSync IPs.
- Sample stream: small subset (we recommend 100–300 docs/day for the shadow).
- Data retention: we will honor your retention policy; artifacts stored in customer bucket for 30 days by default.

Attachments: trial-runbook.pdf (runbook stub with checklist and roles).

I will open a HubSpot task and share a DocuSign SOW draft. If Natalie confirms the hybrid approach today we can start the Day 0 checklist tomorrow morning.

—
Ben Carter
Trial Operations Manager | Redwood Inference

- Share Anika's contact and a short clinical QA checklist for the hallucination audit.

Looking forward to the report and the shadow window.
